H1.text: A ball rolls down a slope and up the other side. A child on a slide speeds up on the way down.

H2.text: Speed comes and goes. Where does it go, and how does it come back?

H3.text: Diya pulls her little cousin's swing back, and lets go.

H4.text: It speeds up, slows down, stops for a moment, and comes back. Nobody pushes it. What keeps it going?

H5.text: By the end of this video, you will predict its speed with one simple rule.

P2.text: It has two parts. Kinetic energy, K, is the energy of motion.

P3.text: Potential energy, U, is energy stored by height, or in a stretched spring.

P4.text: Add them, and you get the mechanical energy, E. E equals K plus U.

P5.text: The rule: if only conservative forces like gravity do work, E never changes. K and U trade places.

S1.text: Let's run it. A twenty kilogram child on a swing, two point five metres long, pulled back to sixty degrees.

S2.text: At the top, the seat is one point two five metres up. U is two hundred and forty five joules. K is zero.

S3.text: Let go. As it swings down, U falls and K rises.

S4.text: At the bottom, U is zero, and K is the full two hundred and forty five joules. Speed: about five metres per second.

S5.text: Up the other side, K turns back into U. It stops at the same height it started from.

S6.text: On the graph, U and K rise and fall, but their sum, E, is a flat line.

S8.text: The rope pulls at right angles to the motion, so it does no work. Only gravity changes the speed.

D1.text: Now the proof, step by step.

D2.text: Step one. The work energy theorem. The work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.

D3.text: Step two. For a conservative force, the work equals minus the change in potential energy.

D4.text: Step three. So delta K equals minus delta U. What K gains, U loses.

D5.text: Step four. Delta K plus delta U equals zero. So K plus U never changes.

D6.text: Step five. Between any two points, K one plus U one equals K two plus U two.

T1.text: Remember this. With only conservative forces at work, K plus U stays the same.

R1.text: So how fast is the seat at the bottom? Follow the links.

R2.text: One. At the top, it is at rest. All its energy is U, m g h.

R3.text: Two. At the bottom, h is zero. All its energy is K, half m v squared.

R4.text: Three. So half m v squared equals m g h. The mass cancels.

R5.text: Four. v equals root two g h. Root of two times nine point eight times one point two five. About four point nine five metres per second.

C2.text: A twenty kilogram child, and a sixty kilogram adult, let go from the same height.

C3.text: At the bottom, the adult has three times the energy. But both move at the same speed.

C4.text: Now you try. Where is the kinetic energy largest: at the top of the swing, or at the bottom? Pause and decide.

C5.text: At the bottom! There the seat is lowest, so U is smallest, and K is largest.

C6.text: One more. A real swing slowly dies down. Is energy being destroyed? Pause and think.

C7.text: No! Air drag and friction at the hooks turn it into heat. The total energy stays the same.

W2.text: A ball is thrown straight down at three metres per second, from a ten metre balcony. How fast does it land? Ignore air.

W3.text: At the top, K one is half m times three squared. U one is m g times ten.

W4.text: At the ground, U two is zero. K two is half m v squared.

W5.text: K one plus U one equals K two. Cancel m. Four point five, plus ninety eight, equals half v squared.

W6.text: So v squared is two hundred and five. v is about fourteen point three metres per second.

X2.text: Many students use K plus U equals constant, even when there is friction.

X3.text: But friction turns some energy into heat. Then K one plus U one equals K two plus U two, plus the heat.

E1.text: Where is this asked? In speed numericals for swings, slopes and falling bodies.

Q1.text: Exam level now. A bob on a one metre string is pulled aside till the string makes sixty degrees with the vertical, and let go. g is ten, cos thirty seven is zero point eight. Find its speed when the string makes thirty seven degrees with the vertical. Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is A. Root six metres per second.

A2.text: It drops L times cos thirty seven minus cos sixty. One times zero point three. Zero point three metres.

A3.text: Half v squared equals g times zero point three. So v squared is two times ten times zero point three. Six.

A4.text: So v is root six, about two point four five metres per second.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. What are the two parts of mechanical energy?

Y3.text: Two. Why do a light child and a heavy adult reach the same speed?

Y4.text: Three. When is mechanical energy not conserved?

N1.text: Next time: press a toy spring gun, and it fires a ball. Where was that energy hiding? Find out in potential energy of a spring.
